raw_text:
Thanks for the detailed client context. Below is a structured 12-week program tailored for a 31-year-old recreational lifter with PCOS (Rotterdam criteria), irregular cycles, HbA1c 5.8, BMI 28, and emphasis on resistance training, body composition, and insulin sensitivity. It avoids crash dieting and excessive cardio, and prioritizes adequate fueling and recovery to support HPA function. The plan assumes access to a full gym.

Overall approach
- Training modality: primarily resistance training with minimal to moderate conditioning to support insulin sensitivity without overtraining.
- Session structure: 4 training days per week (two upper/lower split plus targeted accessory work). Optional 1–2 light cardio or mobility days if energy allows, but not mandatory.
- Progression: linear progression in volume and load within each mesocycle, with deloads every 4th week to manage fatigue and HPA stress.
- Nutrition emphasis: avoid caloric crash dieting. Aim for modest energy balance or slight surplus on training days if goals include body composition improvements. Emphasize protein ~1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight, fiber-rich carbs around workouts, healthy fats, and consistent fueling to support training and insulin sensitivity.
- PCOS considerations: prioritize resistance training, adequate protein, balanced carbs around workouts, and sleep/recovery strategies. Monitor symptoms and adjust as needed.
- Recovery: sleep target 7–9 hours, stress management, hydration, and a plain daily movement baseline to support metabolic health.

Client recognition
- Start date: 2026-06-01.
- Age/sex: 31-year-old female.
- Status: recreational lifter; PCOS; irregular cycle; on endocrinologist guidance; HbA1c 5.8 (prediabetes range); BMI 28.
- Training history: not specified beyond “recreational lifter”—assume consistent resistance training background but not performing a periodized plan currently.
- Safety: no contraindications noted beyond insulin sensitivity/PCOS considerations; consult if any new symptoms.

12-week program: weekly structure
- Week 1–4: Foundation and adaptation (Phase 1). Build technique, establish baseline loads, introduce progressive overload with moderate volume.
- Week 5–8: Hypertrophy and strength (Phase 2). Increase sets/reps and loading, introduce tempo work, prioritize insulin-sensitivity-friendly hypertrophy.
- Week 9–12: Performance and consolidation (Phase 3). Further load progression with reduced reps to focus on strength quality and body recomposition.

Weekly layout (4 training days per week)
- Day A: Lower 1 + core
- Day B: Upper 1
- Day C: Lower 2 + accessory
- Day D: Upper 2
- Optional: 1 light cardio/active recovery day (e.g., 20–30 minutes brisk walk, mobility) or recovery session if energy allows.

Key variables
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week
- Intensity: RPE 7–8 during working sets in early weeks; progress toward RPE 8–9 in later weeks for strength days.
- Tempo: controlled reps (2–0–2–1 for major lifts in hypertrophy weeks; higher emphasis on control for safer progression with PCOS considerations).
- Sets/reps (by week range): 
  - Weeks 1–4: 3–4 sets per main lift; rep ranges 8–12; accessory 2–3 sets of 12–15
  - Weeks 5–8: main lifts 4–5 sets of 6–10; accessories 3–4 sets of 10–14
  - Weeks 9–12: main lifts 4–5 sets of 5–8; accessories 3–4 sets of 8–12
- Reassessment: Week 4 and Week 12 performance benchmarks (3RM assessment for main lifts, or 1RM estimates via projected loads if appropriate).

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation and adaptation)
- Goals: technique mastery, establish baseline loads, safe progression, begin insulin-sensitivity oriented routine.
- Week 1:
  - Day A Lower 1
    - Squat (back squat or goblet if needed): 3 sets x 8 reps at ~65–70% 1RM
    - Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3 x 8
    - Leg Press or Lunges: 3 x 10
    - Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3 x 12
    - Abs: Plank 3 x 30–45s
  - Day B Upper 1
    - Bench or Dumbbell Press: 3 x 8
    - Barbell Row or Dumbbell Row: 3 x 8
    - Overhead Press: 3 x 8
    - Pull-Ups/Assisted Pull-Ups or Lat Pulldown: 3 x 8
    - Triceps pushdown: 3 x 12
    - Banded face pulls: 3 x 15
  - Day C Lower 2
    - Deadlift variant: 3 x 6–8 (conventional or sumo)
    - Front/Back Squat alternative: 3 x 8
    - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3 x 8 per leg
    - Hamstring Curl: 3 x 12
  - Day D Upper 2
    - Incline Dumbbell Press: 3 x 8–10
    - Seated Row: 3 x 8–10
    - Dumbbell Lateral Raise: 3 x 12
    - Chest Flyes: 3 x 12
    - Curls: 3 x 12
- Week 2–4 progression: add 2–5% load where technically feasible, maintain 8–12 rep ranges; add small volume by +1 set for main lifts if tolerated; keep RPE 7–8.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Hypertrophy and strength focus)
- Goals: elevate training stimulus, apply progressive overload, maintain insulin sensitivity focus with higher reps and attention to recovery.
- Week 5–6:
  - Day A Lower 1
    - Squat: 4 x 6–8 at 70–75%
    - RDL: 4 x 6–8
    - Leg Press: 3 x 10
    - Hip Thrust: 3 x 10–12
    - Abs: Hanging leg raises 3 x 10
  - Day B Upper 1
    - Bench: 4 x 6–8
    - Barbell Row: 4 x 6–8
    - Shoulder Press: 3 x 8–10
    - Pull-Ups/Lat Pulldown: 3–4 x 8–10
    - Triceps / Biceps: 3 x 12
  - Day C Lower 2
    - Deadlift: 4 x 5–6
    - Front Squat or Tempo Squat: 3 x 6–8
    - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3 x 8–10
    - Ham Curl: 3 x 10–12
  - Day D Upper 2
    - Incline Press: 4 x 6–8
    - T-Bar Row or Single-Arm Row: 4 x 8–10
    - Lateral Raises: 3 x 12–15
    - Chest Fly or Pec Deck: 3 x 12
    - US curls: 3 x 12
- Week 7–8 progression: add 1–2 reps per set or +2.5–5% load; introduce tempo for some sets (e.g., 3-second eccentric).

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Performance and consolidation)
- Goals: strength-centric with controlled volume, refine body composition.
- Week 9–10:
  - Day A Lower 1
    - Squat: 4–5 x 5–6 at 75–80%
    - RDL: 4 x 6
    - Leg Press: 3 x 8–10
    - Hip Thrust: 3 x 8–10
  - Day B Upper 1
    - Bench: 4–5 x 5–6
    - Barbell Row: 4–5 x 5–6
    - Overhead Press: 3–4 x 6–8
    - Pull-Ups/Lat: 3–4 x 6–8
    - Triceps/Biceps: 3 x 10–12
  - Day C Lower 2
    - Deadlift: 4–5 x 4–6
    - Front Squat: 3–4 x 5–6
    - Split Squat: 3 x 6–8
    - Ham Curl: 3 x 8–10
  - Day D Upper 2
    - Incline Press: 4–5 x 5–6
    - Row: 4–5 x 5–6
    - Lateral Raises: 3 x 12
    - Compound/Isolation accessory: 3 x 8–12
- Week 11–12 deload and test
  - Week 11: Deload week with 50–60% loads, maintain technique.
  - Week 12: Retest main lifts with updated estimated 1RM; adjust final phase goals.

Tempo and technique emphasis
- Primary lifts (squat, hinge, press, row) prioritize controlled eccentric (2–0–2–1) with a strong/conscious concentric.
- Tempo variations: occasional slower eccentrics (e.g., 3–0–3–0) on accessed hypertrophy sets to increase time under tension safely for insulin sensitivity.

Exercise substitutions and progression notes
- If any movement aggravates symptoms or mechanics: swap to a more comfortable alternative (e.g., trap bar deadlift, hip thrust as a substitute for hip extension).
- If access to machines is limited: substitute with barbell-based alternatives and adjust sets/reps accordingly.
- Accessibility: keep a consistent 8–12 rep frame for hypertrophy especially Weeks 1–8; switch to 5–8 reps upper range in Weeks 9–12 for strength emphasis.

Conditioning and cardio
- Conditioning: optional 1–2 sessions per week of low to moderate intensity cardio (20–30 min) if energy/demand allows, with a preference for cycling, incline treadmill walking, or steady-state cardio at conversational pace. Avoid high-volume cardio to protect insulin sensitivity and HPA function.
- Mobility and recovery: 10–15 minutes per session for mobility work targeting hips, thoracic spine, shoulders; add 5–10 minutes of breathing/relaxation techniques post-workout to support HPA balance.

Nutrition and fueling guidance
- Protein: target 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight daily; distribute across 3–4 main meals with a post-workout protein source within 1–2 hours of training (40–60 g protein post-workout depending on tolerance).
- Carbohydrates: prioritize around workouts to support performance and insulin sensitivity; include complex carbohydrates (whole grains, fruits, vegetables) with each meal; avoid long fasting windows; consider 2–3 main fueling periods aligned with training days.
- Fat: maintain healthy fats (nuts, seeds, olive oil, fatty fish) to support satiety and hormonal health.
- Energy balance: avoid strict caloric restriction. If aiming for body recomp, target maintenance or a slight surplus on training days (e.g., +150–250 kcal) and neutral on rest days, with adjustments based on weight trends and energy levels.
- PCOS considerations: emphasize fiber-rich foods, stable blood sugar through balanced meals, and hydration; monitor for signs of energy deficiency, mood changes, or menstrual irregularities.
- Hydration: aim for 30–40 ml/kg/day, more on training days.
- Supplements (if considered): protein supplement to meet daily intake; vitamin D3 if deficient; omega-3 fats; creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day if not contraindicated; ensure medical clearance for any long-term supplementation.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night.
- Stress management: incorporate breathing, mindfulness, or light mobility on rest days.
- Cycle tracking: irregular cycles may complicate exact timings; consider tracking symptoms, mood, energy, and training performance to tailor training around perceived energy and cycle-related symptoms.
- Medical monitoring: continue endocrinology guidance; if cycle regularizes or HbA1c trends improve, adjust plan accordingly.

Program delivery notes
- Each week should include a brief warm-up: 5–10 minutes light cardio, dynamic mobility, and 1–2 activation drills for the primary muscle groups (glutes, hamstrings, thoracic mobility, scapular stability).
- Keep rest intervals: 60–90 seconds for most sets; 2–3 minutes for main compound lifts as needed when heavy.
- 4-week cycle with built-in deloads: Weeks 4, 8, and 12 (or 4, 8, 11) feature reduced volume/intensity to support recovery.

Safety and monitoring
- If fatigue, excessive soreness, or deteriorating energy persists, reduce volume by 20–30% and extend rest days.
- If symptoms of overtraining or significant menstrual disturbance occur, pause high-intensity sessions and consult healthcare provider.

Please let me know:
- The client’s weight, height, and current estimated 1RM or best working weights for the major lifts (squat, deadlift, bench press) to tailor loads precisely.
- Any injuries or movement limitations.
- Weekly schedule availability and preferred training times.
- Any dietary restrictions or preferences so I can tailor nutrition targets more precisely.
